analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infrastructures is a small civil construction contractor with no meaningful R&D, no proprietary technology, and a lumpy project-based revenue model — the antithesis of the innovation-driven compounders I seek. Revenue has flattened (97→90 Cr) and ROE of 13.6% falls well short of my 20%+ threshold, making the 26x P/E unjustified.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 72.38% signals long-term commitment
Deleveraging evident: borrowings down 109→60 Cr while equity grew 11→116 Cr
Operating margins expanded from ~15% to ~27% (Op Income 13→24 Cr)
key_risks: Revenue decelerating — FY25 revenue dropped 7% to 90 Cr vs peak 97 Cr
Civil construction is a bid-driven commodity business with zero innovation moat
OCF collapsed from 32 Cr (FY24) to 5 Cr (FY25), hinting at working-capital stress
red_flags: Growth decelerating/reversing on a tiny revenue base
No R&D spend — fails my innovation test entirely
FY25 equity jump (27→116 Cr) suggests dilutive fundraise post-IPO
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying my 15-point checklist, this company fails on the most critical dimensions. There is no R&D pipeline, no sales organization with durable advantages, no proprietary process, and no product with multi-year growth runway beyond project wins. The 348% 3-year CAGR is a base-effect illusion (FY22 revenue was 1 Cr); the real story is FY23→FY25 where revenue went 89→97→90 Cr — essentially flat with a decline in the latest year. That is precisely the "growth decelerating" red flag I warn against.

At 26x earnings on 13 Cr of net profit, the market is pricing this like a quality compounder when the economics are pedestrian: ROE 13.6%, ROCE 15.5%, and FCF of just 2 Cr in FY25. Civil construction in India is hyper-competitive, cyclical, working-capital intensive, and offers no scuttlebutt edge — customers (government/developers) are price-driven, suppliers are commoditized, and competitors are legion. I would pass without hesitation and redeploy capital into businesses with genuine innovation capacity.
